results: 1. Full dermatologic skin examination with dermoscopy
skin examination: a painless, non-pruritic confluent erythematous rash on the left arm one day before the chorea began; it improved with doxycycline and clindamycin but the chorea did not
2. KOH preparation of any scaly or suspicious lesions
3. Wood's lamp examination of the affected skin
4. Punch biopsy of the most representative skin lesion for histopathology
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: normal
TSH, free T4 and free T3: normal
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Sydenham chorea (acute rheumatic fever) following Group A Streptococcal skin infection (erysipelas)

Alternatives to consider:
1. Lyme disease with neuroborreliosis causing chorea (erythema migrans on the arm; doxycycline would treat early skin involvement but established CNS disease requires IV ceftriaxone, explaining persistent chorea)
2. Post-streptococcal autoimmune chorea / PANDAS-spectrum disorder
3. Infective endocarditis with cutaneous septic emboli and embolic/immune-mediated chorea (less likely given absence of fever)
